findings.description: The bucket has no configured default server-side encryption. Although S3 now applies SSE-S3 automatically for new uploads, this configuration does not explicitly enforce encryption or a customer-managed KMS key as a security control.
The bucket has no configured default server-side encryption. Its private ACL restricts access but does not establish or enforce an encryption-at-rest control for ledger exports.
The bucket has no configured default server-side encryption. Versioning and access logging do not encrypt stored model artifacts.
The bucket has no configured default server-side encryption, leaving encryption of runbook content dependent on S3 service defaults or uploader behavior rather than an explicit bucket control.

The object upload does not request server-side encryption and its destination bucket has no explicit default encryption configuration. The vendor roster is therefore not protected by an explicit Terraform-managed encryption control.
